lesson.title: Role-Play: Greeting the Principal and a Teammate
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: You've sorted people into tú and usted on paper — now it's time to actually say the words out loud in two very different situations: greeting your school principal, and greeting a teammate.

[[¿cómo está usted?]] literally means 'how are you,' asked in the formal register — you'll hear adults use it with teachers, principals, doctors, and anyone else they're showing respect to. Its informal twin is ¿cómo estás?, which you already know from tú conversations. Same question, same meaning, different level of politeness — exactly like the difference between 'how's it going?' and 'how are you doing today?' in English.

Set up two 'stations' around the room (or just two chairs) and act out both scenes, with a family member playing the second role each time.

STATION 1 — Greeting the principal (formal):
ESTUDIANTE: Buenos días, señora directora. ¿Cómo está usted?
DIRECTORA: Muy bien, gracias. ¿Y usted?
ESTUDIANTE: Bien, gracias.

STATION 2 — Greeting a teammate (informal):
TÚ: ¡Hola! ¿Cómo estás?
AMIGO: Bien, ¿y tú?
TÚ: Muy bien, gracias.

After you perform both, build your own greeting exchange from scrambled words in the activity below — same two exchanges, jumbled up.

You just performed the same basic exchange — a greeting and a reply — in two completely different registers. Tomorrow you'll read short written conversations and figure out, just from the words on the page, whether each one is formal or informal.

objectives: Perform a formal greeting exchange (¿Cómo está usted?) and an informal greeting exchange (¿Cómo estás?) aloud from memory
Reassemble scrambled words into a correct greeting sentence in either register
materialsNeeded: Two chairs or taped-off areas to mark 'stations'
A family member to play the second role
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review ¿Cómo estás? from Day 1 and introduce ¿Cómo está usted? as its formal twin.
2. Set up two stations (or just two spots in the room).
3. Act out Station 1 (principal, formal) together, then Station 2 (teammate, informal), swapping who plays which role.
4. Have the child do the word-order building activity, building each line of both exchanges from scrambled words.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's reading activity.
differentiationTips: Struggling: let them read the dialogue lines directly off the page for the first run-through before asking them to perform from memory
Ready for more: have them improvise a third exchange — greeting a new adult neighbor (usted) — using only the patterns they already know
Ham it up: exaggerating a stiff, formal posture for usted lines and a relaxed, casual posture for tú lines helps the register distinction stick physically, not just verbally
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Formal greeting to the principal: Buenos días, señora directora. ¿Cómo está usted? 2. Informal greeting to a teammate: ¡Hola! ¿Cómo estás? 3. Formal 'how are you': ¿Cómo está usted? 4. Informal 'how are you': ¿Cómo estás?
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Moves the week's WA-WL-2015.1.1 Interpersonal Communication target from recognition (Days 1-2) to spoken production — the scope-and-sequence specifically calls for role-play stations here so the register choice becomes something the student can actually perform, not just identify.

rows.problem: Write the formal greeting you'd use to say hello to your school principal.
Write the informal greeting you'd use to say hello to a teammate.
Write the formal way to ask 'How are you?' to an adult you respect.
Write the informal way to ask 'How are you?' to a friend.
